newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end lower, but avoid Dow losses.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end lower, but avoid Dow losses.

* Toronto stocks ended weaker on Tuesday, but avoided Dow's steep decline * Strong conglomerates restrained losses in banking, gold, consumer products * 97 million shares traded
Toronto stocks ended weaker on Tuesday, but strength in conglomerates helped the Canadian market avoid Wall Street's steep decline.
The TSE 300 Composite Index fell 31.87 points to finish at 6808.50. Trading was brisk with volume of 97.28 million shares worth C$1.52 billion.

On Wall Street, the Dow Jones average sank more than 101 points on data suggesting U.S. economic growth was accelerating. "The Johnson Redbook came out and immediately the market went into the tank," said Rolie Bradley, an institutional salesman at Maison Placements Canada Inc.
The Redbook report was up by 0.9 percent in the first week of August as retailers said sales were better than expected.

U.S. and Canadian debt markets weakened on the report, while nervous investors awaited U.S. July retail sales data due on Wednesday. Canada's 30-year bond fell C$0.71 to C$117.10 to yield 6.609 percent.

The only bright spot for Toronto equities was the conglomerates group, which restrained heavy losses in financial services, consumer products and utilities. Declining issues outpointed advances 498 to 488, with 298 stocks unchanged.
--- HOT STOCKS ---

* Repap Enterprises Inc edged up 0.03 to 0.26 on 14 million shares, the TSE's heaviest trader. Silverton International Fund Ltd and Paloma Partners LLC, which own about 29 percent of Repap's common shares, said on Tuesday they would combine forces to change Repap's management and board of directors.
* Canadian Pacific Ltd lifted the conglomerates group. CP gained 0.75 to 41. It announced plans to buy back up to 18 million, or 5.3 percent, of its common shares.
* Falconbridge Ltd fell 1.10 to 27.70 as the strike at its Sudbury, Ontario operations dragged on.
